pageProps.title: Greenhouse at the End of the World
pageProps.review: A reading review of Kim Cho-yeop's SF novel set in a world on the brink of destruction due to lethal toxic nano-dust, examining the dual nature of humans contained in the survival of mankind and the sacrifice of resistant species.
pageProps.description: 60 years after the reconstruction following human extinction, a mysterious email arrives from someone claiming to know the truth about the suddenly multiplying blue light plants
pageProps.content:
## Review A story of a generation on the brink of extinction due to a lethal toxic nano-dust called ```Dust```. A common subject in SF is indeed the extinction of mankind. If the production is possible, it seems like a material and fun element that could be made into a movie.
The duality of mankind in dealing with the resistant species that always appears in such stories is also revealed in this book. Are they beings that must be sacrificed for the sake of mankind and the public interest?
